preceding_messages.text: I adopt the GPS-triple re-keying and the exclusion of serial number as an interval boundary verbatim; they give the suppression span a physical referent that survives the hardware being carried two metres north. Because a ±0.5 m GPS report in a dense neighborhood is subject to multipath jitter of two to three metres that can converge on the same lobe at similar times of day, I mandate that each coordinate survey—old and new—be fixed by a second method: a transect measurement from the site's commissioning-day reference peg (a stainless-steel dowel driven to bedrock, marked in the horizon-sketch appendix) to the instrument mounting point, recorded to ±2 cm, and that the suppression-interval boundary is defined by the transect offset rather than by the raw GPS report. The failure this closes: at 18:00 Tuesday the crew's handheld receiver resolves under clear western sky to old-coordinate +2 m east, while at 06:00 Thursday it resolves under dawn multipath from a glass office façade to new-coordinate −1 m north, and the reported triples differ by only 0.4 m—inside the ±0.5 m resolution threshold—so the interval collapses to zero and Wednesday's 0.57 hPa spread executes an immediate audit dispatch against a survey already retired by Tuesday's relocation order, printing the same confusing duplicate appendix entry your example describes. I therefore require that any week in which the transect-measured offset and the raw GPS delta disagree by more than 1.5 m triggers a survey-quality annotation "TRIPLES DISCORDANT — INTERVAL DEFINED BY TRANSECT" in the suppression note, so the interval's physical extent is always anchored to the peg geometry and the GPS report serves only as corroborating metadata in the appendix rather than as the operative boundary.

preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the transect-offset boundary definition, the commissioning-day reference peg, and the "TRIPLES DISCORDANT — INTERVAL DEFINED BY TRANSECT" annotation verbatim; they anchor the suppression interval to sub-centimetre physical geometry that GPS multipath cannot collapse below the relocation threshold. Because the peg is now the single physical referent for the entire interval-suppression protocol, its integrity must be independently corroborated: at commissioning the peg is cross-checked to a painted datum mark on an adjacent immovable structure (a utility-pole base or building corner) to ±5 mm, and every weekly observation session begins with a ten-second visual confirmation that the peg head is present and undisturbed. The concrete failure this closes: Site 3's peg sits beneath a parking-lot resurfacing in week 9, the asphalt contractor fractures the dowel above bedrock but leaves it embedded, and over a summer of thermal cycling the peg head shifts 6 mm laterally—irrelevant to pressure but sufficient to corrupt any transect-dependent interval calculation that assumes the peg is at its commissioning coordinate, so that a subsequent genuine relocation measured from the drifted peg yields a suppression span shorter than the true physical gap and the inter-site audit trigger executes against an already-relocated site. I therefore mandate that if the weekly visual check finds the peg absent or displaced more than 5 mm from its painted datum, the transect is suspended, the interval definition reverts to the conservative worst case (the full span between the two raw GPS triples, however large), and the suppression note prints "PEG COMPROMISED — INTERVAL UNDEFINED — CONSERVATIVE SPAN APPLIED" so that every queued audit trigger is held in queue rather than executed during the ambiguous span.

target.speaker: X
target.text: I adopt the commissioning datum cross-check, the ten-second weekly visual confirmation, and the "PEG COMPROMISED — INTERVAL UNDEFINED — CONSERVATIVE SPAN APPLIED" conservative-span fallback verbatim; they give the suppression interval a defined worst-case boundary when the peg's integrity is in question. Because a painted datum mark on a utility-pole base is a municipal-maintenance asset subject to annual repaint cycles, I mandate that the datum be replaced by a 2 mm stainless dowel-pin driven 10 mm into the structure at commissioning and tagged in the horizon-sketch appendix with a micro-etch serial, and that any weekly visual check finding the pin absent—rather than displaced—degrades the integrity test to a monthly full-transect re-measurement against the commissioning-day stored offset, with any delta exceeding 1 mm triggering the same "PEG COMPROMISED" annotation and conservative-span application. The concrete failure this closes: the painted datum on Site 3's pole base is removed by a municipal repaint in week 14, the weekly check finds the peg head present and logs a pass, but no displacement measurement is possible for the eight weeks until the city repaints; during that window thermal cycling drifts the peg laterally, and a week-22 relocation's transect—referenced to the drifted peg—assigns a suppression span four hours shorter than the true physical gap, so the inter-site pressure-spread trigger executes an immediate elevation-recording audit against an already-relocated coordinate and prints the duplicate appendix entry a year-two resident reads as procedural incoherence. I therefore require that any week in which the datum pin is absent prints "DATUM ABSENT — INTEGRITY UNRESOLVED — CONSERVATIVE SPAN APPLIED" in the suppression note and holds all queued inter-site audit triggers in queue until the monthly transect re-measurement either confirms peg integrity within 1 mm or retires the peg under the full relocation-review protocol.
